SECTION 0. ANALYSIS OVERVIEW
────────────────────────────
What changed since the pack's fiscal-year data: BioMarin closed the Amicus
Therapeutics acquisition on 2026-04-27 for ~$4.8B all-cash ($14.50/sh)
[Actual, company PR + 8-K]. It added GALAFOLD (Fabry) and POMBILITI+OPFOLDA
(Pompe) plus US rights to BMN 820 (FSGS, Ph3). The pack's FY2025 balance
sheet (cash $1.312B, vendor debt $0.606B) is PRE-merger and is NOT the live
capital structure. The deal was financed with $4.25B: $850M 5.5% senior
notes due 2034 + $2.8B senior secured term loan + $600M revolver [Actual,
Cooley PR 2026-04-27]. Post-merger net debt is therefore materially higher
than the pack implies — estimated ~$3.5B [Estimate].

Second, a direct competitor entered: Ascendis Pharma's YUVIWEL (navepegritide),
once-WEEKLY for achondroplasia, was FDA-approved 2026-02-27 and commercially
available early Q2 2026 [Actual, Ascendis PR / FDA]. It now competes head-to-
head with VOXZOGO (daily). This is the single largest fundamental risk to the
flagship and is already live at T0.

Third, the ITC case direction in the research brief is INVERTED. BioMarin is
the COMPLAINANT (it sued Ascendis for infringing VOXZOGO patent RE48,267);
Ascendis is the respondent [Actual, Justia/Fed Cir. 26-1026, Patently-O].
An adverse ITC outcome for BioMarin means NO exclusion order — i.e., Yuviwel
remains on the market. A FAVORABLE outcome would exclude Yuviwel. The brief's
claim that an exclusion order "could impact market exclusivity for VOXZOGO"
is wrong; it would block the competitor, not BioMarin's product. ITC final
decision expected Dec 2026 [Estimate, secondary].

Net: this is a FCF-positive rare-disease compounder that (a) just levered up
~$3.65B to buy growth, and (b) just lost its achondroplasia franchise to a
structurally more convenient competitor, with a Dec-2026 legal event that
partially determines the competitive outcome.

Model confidence: MODERATE. Tier-1 (filed) data is solid for history; the
forward path leans on Tier-3/4 (guidance, [Assumption] margins, [Unconfirmed]
PPA/SBC/post-merger BS). Confidence is downgraded accordingly.

SECTION 3.5. SECOND-ORDER EFFECTS

Step 3.5-1. Competitive response: Ascendis (Yuviwel, weekly) will compete on
convenience — a STRUCTURAL advantage over daily VOXZOGO, not a temporary one.
If BMRN WINS the ITC (Dec 2026), Yuviwel is excluded from the US (impact +3).
If BMRN LOSES, Yuviwel stays and erodes share (impact −2 to −3). Other CNP
entrants are secondary. Net competitive impact is the dominant swing factor.
Step 3.5-2. Reflexivity: Positive — a higher stock price is M&A currency
(used for Amicus) and aids talent retention. Negative — a lower price raises
funding cost, but BMRN is FCF-positive so it is NOT funding-dependent (mild
reflexivity, not a survival issue).
Step 3.5-3. Customer behavior: Rare-disease patients are effectively "late
adopters" who REQUIRE therapy (high LTV, low churn) — UNTIL a more convenient
competitor appears. Yuviwel's entry raises switching/churn risk in ACH
specifically; LTV/CAC improve as VOXZOGO penetrates <20% of its addressable
market [Actual, company] but the ceiling is now contested.
